'''Rainer Froese''' (born 25 August 1950 in [[Wismar]], [[East Germany]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.futureocean.org/prop/froese.pdf |title=Curriculum of Research |last1=Utecht |first1=Christine |date=10 March 2006 |website=[[The Future Ocean]] |publisher=[[Leibniz Institute of Marine Sciences]] |accessdate=19 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219192403/http://www.futureocean.org/prop/froese.pdf |archive-date=19 December 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref>) is a senior [[scientist]] at the Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research (GEOMAR) in [[Kiel]], formerly the [[Leibniz Institute of Marine Sciences]] (IFM-GEOMAR), and a Pew Fellow in Marine Conservation.<ref name=Pew>[http://www.pewenvironment.org/research-programs/marine-fellow/id/8589941905 Marine Fellow: Rainer Froese] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131221164050/http://www.pewenvironment.org/research-programs/marine-fellow/id/8589941905 |date=21 December 2013 }} ''Pew Environment Group''.</ref> He obtained an MSc in Biology in 1985 at the [[University of Kiel]] and a PhD in Biology in 1990 from the [[University of Hamburg]]. Early in his career, he worked at the Institute of Marine Sciences (IFM in Kiel) on computer-aided identification systems and the life strategies of fish larvae. His current research interests include fish information systems, [[marine biodiversity]], marine [[biogeography]], and the [[population dynamics of fisheries]] and [[large marine ecosystem]]s.<ref name=Pew />

Froese is best known for his work developing and maintaining [[FishBase]], a large and widely accessed online information system on fish.<ref name=Pew /> From 1990 until 2000, Froese lead the development of [[FishBase]] at [[ICLARM]] in Manila. Since 2000, he has coordinated the large international consortium that now oversees FishBase.<ref>[http://na.oceana.org/en/our-work/promote-responsible-fishing/fishing-subsidies/learn-act/dr-rainer-froese Dr. Rainer Froese] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110602123317/http://na.oceana.org/en/our-work/promote-responsible-fishing/fishing-subsidies/learn-act/dr-rainer-froese |date=2 June 2011 }} ''Oceania''. Retrieved 15 July 2011.</ref> Its searchable database contains 34,000 fish species and the site receives over 30 million views each month.<ref>[http://www.fishbase.org/search.php FishBase] – main web page.</ref> He is also the coordinator of [[AquaMaps]], which produces computer-generated global distribution maps for marine species,<ref>[http://www.aquamaps.org/main/home.php AquaMaps] – home web page</ref> and science adviser to [[SeaLifeBase]], which is an extension of FishBase to aquatic organisms other than fish.<ref>[http://www.sealifebase.org/home/pages/partners.htm Sealifebase: Partners] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110803171839/http://www.sealifebase.org/home/pages/partners.htm |date=3 August 2011 }} Updated 30 September 2010. Retrieved 18 July 2011.</ref><ref>[http://www.sealifebase.org/home/pages/index.htm Sealifebase: Home] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110814093158/http://www.sealifebase.org/home/pages/index.htm |date=14 August 2011 }} Updated 30 September 2010. Retrieved 18 July 2011.</ref>

Froese has authored or co-authored over 100 scientific publications.<ref>[http://www.fin.ph/board-of-trustees.html Board of Trustees] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120730182348/http://www.fin.ph/board-of-trustees.html |date=30 July 2012 }}, FishBase Information and Research Group. Retrieved 15 July 2011.</ref> In 1998, along with [[Daniel Pauly]] and others, Froese authored an influential paper called ''[[Fishing down marine food webs]]''.<ref name=fdtmfw>[[Daniel Pauly|Pauly D]], [[Villy Christensen|Christensen V]], Dalsgaard J, Froese R and Torres F (1998) [http://www.fisheries.ubc.ca/members/dpauly/journalArticles/1998/FishingDownMarineFoodWebs.pdf "Fishing down marine food webs"] ''Science'', '''279''': 860–863.</ref> The paper examined the consequences of preferentially targeting large [[predator fish]] over smaller [[forage fish]]. As a result, the [[fishing industry]] has been "[[fishing down the food web]]", and the [[mean trophic level]] in the oceans has progressively decreased. More recently, in a 2011 letter to ''Nature'', he stated that the European [[Common Fisheries Policy]] "consistently gets to overrule scientific advice and drive fish stocks to the brink of collapse. Without massive subsidies, European fisheries would be bankrupt: the cost of hunting the few remaining fish would exceed the income from selling the catch."<ref>Froese R (2011) [http://www.nature.com/news/2011/110706/full/475007a.html "Fishery reform slips through the net"] '' Nature'', Letter, '''475''': 7. {{doi|10.1038/475007a}} [http://www.fishbase.de/rfroese/FishingEdge6.pdf Expanded version]</ref>
